non_low_risk_members: unifi__connector_network_get: Generic GET proxy for the UniFi Network application: the caller supplies the console id and the sub-path under the Cloud Connector proxy prefix, and the raw upstream response is returned. The upstream restricts the request to GET and validates every path segment against traversal, but the endpoint itself is caller-selected, so group membership cannot constrain which UniFi endpoint is read. It is narrower than court-listener__call_endpoint, which also exposes the HTTP method, but it is the same shape: a caller-chosen target. In this deployment the tool is additionally inert, because UNIFI_SITE_MANAGER_ENABLED is unset and the call raises 'Site Manager API is not enabled'.

unifi__connector_protect_get: Generic GET proxy for the UniFi Protect application: the caller supplies the console id and the sub-path under the Cloud Connector proxy prefix, and the raw upstream response is returned. The upstream restricts the request to GET and validates every path segment against traversal, but the endpoint itself is caller-selected, so group membership cannot constrain which Protect endpoint is read, including the camera and event endpoints. In this deployment the tool is additionally inert, because UNIFI_SITE_MANAGER_ENABLED is unset and the call raises 'Site Manager API is not enabled'.

unifi__fleet_fanout: Runs one caller-named read tool across every controller in scope at once. The upstream enforces that only read-tier controller tools can be fanned out and rejects fleet-prefixed and unknown tool names, so the effect class is bounded to reads, but the caller still chooses which tool runs: a holder of this tool reaches every read-tier controller tool whether or not that tool is in the group it was granted. Group membership therefore cannot constrain the target, which is the property that makes a tool broad-capability rather than an ordinary read.

tools.reason: Generic REST client for arbitrary CourtListener API endpoints. Opens or reuses a live browser session and can run browser code against authenticated third-party sites. The session survives between calls and the code it runs is caller-supplied, so the effect class is not bounded by the tool. Treated as broad capability rather than a page-reading helper.

Creates a new project inside the operator's external Framer SaaS account. It is persistent third-party state creation with no verified Noesis consumer, so granting it would add an unreviewed external surface for no workflow benefit.

Executes a caller-supplied JavaScript program that mutates a Framer project. This is arbitrary code execution against a third-party SaaS project; the arguments bound the effect, not the class of effect.

Runs one caller-selected GitBook API operation discovered through search, with caller-supplied path, query and body parameters. The upstream states that the operation surface includes actions that are visible to the public or cannot be undone, such as publishing a site or merging a change request, so the caller chooses the target and therefore the effect class. This is the same shape as court-listener__call_endpoint, and the curated GitBook tools are not a constraint on what it can reach.

Generic GET proxy for the UniFi Network application: the caller supplies the console id and the sub-path under the Cloud Connector proxy prefix, and the raw upstream response is returned. The upstream restricts the request to GET and validates every path segment against traversal, but the endpoint itself is caller-selected, so group membership cannot constrain which UniFi endpoint is read. It is narrower than court-listener__call_endpoint, which also exposes the HTTP method, but it is the same shape: a caller-chosen target. In this deployment the tool is additionally inert, because UNIFI_SITE_MANAGER_ENABLED is unset and the call raises 'Site Manager API is not enabled'.

Generic GET proxy for the UniFi Protect application: the caller supplies the console id and the sub-path under the Cloud Connector proxy prefix, and the raw upstream response is returned. The upstream restricts the request to GET and validates every path segment against traversal, but the endpoint itself is caller-selected, so group membership cannot constrain which Protect endpoint is read, including the camera and event endpoints. In this deployment the tool is additionally inert, because UNIFI_SITE_MANAGER_ENABLED is unset and the call raises 'Site Manager API is not enabled'.

Runs one caller-named read tool across every controller in scope at once. The upstream enforces that only read-tier controller tools can be fanned out and rejects fleet-prefixed and unknown tool names, so the effect class is bounded to reads, but the caller still chooses which tool runs: a holder of this tool reaches every read-tier controller tool whether or not that tool is in the group it was granted. Group membership therefore cannot constrain the target, which is the property that makes a tool broad-capability rather than an ordinary read.

unsupported_requested_categories.reason: No DevOps or CI server is registered in this gateway. There is no Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, cloud-provider or CI tool among the 700 discovered tools. The nearest surfaces are workflow-inspection, observability and the network-* groups, and naming any of them 'devops-readonly' would misrepresent it: they report state, they do not change infrastructure. Infrastructure execution lives in the noesis-ansible repository and in the Hermes terminal toolset, not in MCPJungle.

The UniFi MCP server is registered in this gateway and contributes 212 read tools, split across seven groups by capability: network-inventory, network-security-policy, network-telemetry, network-protect, network-fleet, network-backup and network-controller, plus network-proxy which is held review-required. The deployment sets UNIFI_READ_ONLY=true, so the registered surface contains no mutating UniFi tool at all: these groups are a read-only view by construction, not by policy. Note that the separately-configured Hermes connection 'unifi-local' exposes 347 tools including mutating ones and is NOT constrained by any group here.

The Cloudflare account is now registered (servers cloudflare, cloudflare-agents-sdk, cloudflare-blog, cloudflare-browser, cloudflare-docs). Read-only coverage is the cloudflare-docs-and-blog-read group (docs/blog/Agents-SDK/Pages-migration search) and the cloudflare-browser-render group (fetch/render a caller-chosen URL through Cloudflare's Browser Rendering service, held medium risk). This is a documentation and browser-rendering surface, not a Cloudflare zone/DNS/account-configuration read; no server here reads live zone, DNS, WAF or account settings.

Still a genuine gap for zone/DNS/account CONFIGURATION writes: no registered server exposes Cloudflare zone, DNS, WAF, Workers deployment or account-settings mutation. cloudflare__execute (held review-required, out of all groups, in unassigned_review_required) can reach the full Cloudflare REST API including these writes, but it is a generic code-execution dispatcher with no verified Noesis consumer, not curated write coverage -- granting it would not close this gap safely.
No blockchain, wallet, miner or DePIN data server is registered. The noesis-ledger domain can only be served by the generic web-research, academic-research and market-research groups.

No spending, transfer, trading, payment or wallet tool exists anywhere in the 700-tool inventory. Hunter's credit-consuming lookups draw on a metered search and credit quota rather than money, and the connected account is on the free tier; on a paid plan the same calls would become billable, which is why the spending constraint is recorded on hunter-contact-records rather than treated as absent. The one payment-adjacent tool is court-listener__pray_for_document, which sits in legal-alerts under a spending control.

No mail, chat or SMS server is registered in this gateway. The communications read surfaces are the Mintlify comment thread and the Notion calendar, which together are not an inbox: the Herald workflow still cannot read prior outbound correspondence, and no tool here can confirm what was already sent to anyone.

n8n data tables, the Mintlify deployment databases and the Notion data sources provide readable and writable tabular surfaces, and the groups exist. There is still no generic SQL database server (no PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite tool). The two SQL surfaces present are each confined to its own store: mintlify__query_analytics is held in data-analytics, and the Notion queries in notion-data-query are read-only by construction.

Deployment status, workflow run history, execution records, provider credit and usage reporting, and the Hunter quota report cover the original read-only observability surface. Two BetterStack monitoring accounts are now registered: betterstack-noesis-monitoring-read (the operator's own account: uptime monitors, heartbeats, incidents, dashboards, charts, logs and metrics queries) and betterstack-ryno-monitoring-read (a separate human operator's account, read-only; write/destructive coverage of that same account sits in betterstack-ryno-monitoring-operate and betterstack-ryno-monitoring-destructive, both held with no default Noesis consumer). This closes most of the metrics/log-aggregation gap for application and uptime monitoring; there is still no infrastructure-level telemetry server (no Prometheus, Grafana or Loki) registered, and the UniFi groups still report controller state as read by the controller, not as collected telemetry.

n8n provides agent draft authoring, versioning, validation and retirement; the Beacon-managed server provides the memory and trace substrate agents read from; and Notion provides Custom Agent sessions plus the skill enablement that decides what those agents may load. All three surfaces exist, and the groups exist.

Only two genuine security surfaces exist: GitHub secret scanning and Beacon's security findings. There is no SAST, DAST, dependency-audit or container-scanning server registered, so the group cannot cover a full security review. The UniFi groups read the operator's own security posture but are not a scanning surface.
The GitHub MCP server exposes both surfaces, split across source-control-readonly, source-control-issues-readonly and source-control-write. It is the only source-control server registered.

Hunter registers 103 tools covering contact discovery, enrichment, CRM record management and outbound email sending, split across six groups. The sending surface is isolated in hunter-outbound-email, and the destructive record surface in hunter-record-destructive. This is the only registered capability that sends email to people who did not ask to be contacted, so it carries the strictest approval control in the catalog.

Notion contributes 65 tools covering the operator's own workspace (pages, databases, comments, calendars and agent sessions) and GitBook contributes 12 covering the operator's own GitBook organization (sites, navigation, change requests and publication). The two are split by capability and by risk, and neither can be confused with the MISJustice/YWCA GitBook corpus, which stays in legal-research.
